limits: Writes to the notebook held in this browser.
bio.jane/contract.noScientificClaim: Stores the user's text; computes nothing.
bio.jane/contract.question: Write this text into the lab notebook.

description: Write what just happened into your lab notebook: a new entry, or more text appended to one you name. The body is markdown and its @plasmid / !action / &gel references are extracted as you write, so an entry made by a run is cross-linked exactly like one you typed — and carries the `automated` tag, so you can always tell which is which. Use it to end a pipeline with a record of itself instead of a reminder to write one.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

body_md.description: the entry body, markdown. `@plasmid-name`, `!action-id` and `&gel-id` references in it are extracted into the entry's cross-reference lists, which is what makes a notebook searchable by construct.

collection.description: file it in this collection, creating the collection if it does not exist — the notebook's own grouping, the same one the panel lists.

entry_id.description: append to this entry instead of creating one — the id `list_experiments` returns. A pipeline that runs twice should append to its own entry rather than leaving two.

tags.description: tags to file it under, beyond the `automated` tag every entry written here carries.

title.description: the entry title. A new entry needs one. On an append, giving a title RENAMES the experiment, so leave it out to keep the name it has.

name: record_experiment

bodyChars.description: the stored body length. The engine caps a body at 1,000,000 bytes, so a long append can be shorter here than what was sent — read it rather than assuming the write was whole

collection.description: the collection it is filed in, or an empty string when it is filed in none

created.description: true for a new entry, false when text was appended to an existing one

crossRefs.description: the @plasmid / !action / &gel references the engine extracted from the body — empty lists are a real answer and mean the body named no construct, which is worth noticing in an entry about one

entry_id.description: the entry written — pass it back to append to this same experiment next time

tags.description: the tags as stored, including `automated` — the engine caps and cleans these, so read them back rather than assuming

unresolved.description: `{ references, citations }`: every `@` / `!` / `&` reference in the stored body that names nothing in this workspace, as written, and every citation key that is not a DOI, PMID or PMCID. Empty lists mean every reference resolves; fix and append when they are not. Null when the write ran without the check (a blocking workflow run)
